prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments (policy-only)

- Fiscal and tax: Cut the deficit every year; aim for current budget surplus and falling national debt; no new borrowing for pledges; independent auditing of manifestos by the budget watchdog; cap structural welfare spending. Reintroduce a 50p top income tax rate; create a 10p tax band; no rises in basic/higher Income Tax, National Insurance or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close avoidance loopholes; require public beneficial-ownership registers in relevant territories.

- Economy and infrastructure: Independent National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 and better northern rail, strategic roads, cycling; swift decision on extra runway capacity; long-term science funding; nationwide high-speed broadband and improved mobile coverage. Decarbonise electricity by 2030; empower the Green Investment Bank; establish an Energy Security Board; robust regulation for onshore unconventional gas; long-term strategy for offshore oil and gas.

- Business and markets: Small Business Administration; cut and freeze business rates for small firms; British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition; levy on payday lenders to boost credit unions. Reform corporate governance (long-term investor duties, takeover voting rules, public interest test, employee voice on pay committees).

- Work and skills: Raise the minimum wage to over £8 by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and first‑year tax rebates; require listed firms to report on Living Wage status. Ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts (12‑week regular-hours right); end agency undercutting; abolish employment tribunal fees.

- Young people: Cut university tuition fees to £6,000; curb unpaid internships; guarantee a paid job for long‑term young unemployed (bank bonus tax funded). Guarantee an apprenticeship for qualified school leavers; expand public‑sector apprenticeships; focus apprenticeships at Level 3+, minimum two years; create Technical Degrees; introduce a Youth Allowance linked to training.

- Consumers: Freeze household energy bills until 2017 while reforming the market (separate generation and supply, simpler tariffs, stronger regulator); energy‑efficiency loans and upgrades; decency standard for private rentals. Water affordability scheme and stronger regulator. Rail franchising reform; allow a public operator; one‑year fare freeze then caps; right to the cheapest ticket; local powers over buses and smart ticketing.

- Health and care: Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives (funded by a mansion tax, tobacco levy, anti‑avoidance); 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer diagnostics; integrate physical, mental and social care; mental health parity, quicker access to talking therapies; public health measures on activity, alcohol and children’s food marketing; stronger safety and professional regulation.

- Social care and carers: End 15‑minute visits; year‑of‑care budgets; recruit 5,000 home‑care workers; identify and support unpaid carers; ring‑fence carers’ breaks; support a cap on care costs.

- Education: Protect the whole education budget; strengthen vocational route with a Technical Baccalaureate and Institutes of Technical Education; English/Maths to 18; independent careers advice; all teachers qualified; new leadership and teaching standards; local Directors of School Standards; cap infant class sizes; link private‑school reliefs to state‑sector partnerships; compulsory age‑appropriate SRE.

- Families and housing: Expand free childcare to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4s; wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave and increase pay. Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first‑time buyers in growth areas; land transparency and “use it or lose it”; back small builders and garden cities; three‑year private tenancies with rent‑rise ceilings; ban letting fees; landlord register; tackle homelessness.

- Welfare, disability, older people: Keep the household benefit cap (review regional levels); tailored back‑to‑work support with mandatory skills training; pause and review Universal Credit; higher JSA for contributors; abolish the Bedroom Tax; reform the Work Capability Assessment and provide specialist support. Retain the state pension triple lock; protect key pensioner benefits (with means‑testing for winter fuel at the top end); reform pensions market and guidance.

- Immigration: +1,000 border staff (funded by a small charge on non‑visa visitors); full exit checks; tighter short‑term study visas; maintain the non‑EU work cap; English requirement for public‑facing roles; two‑year wait for most benefit claims; enforce fair hiring (no overseas‑only recruitment; extend gangmasters remit); end indefinite detention for specified vulnerable groups; uphold asylum obligations, including for vulnerable Syrian refugees.

- Policing, justice, extremism: Protect neighbourhood policing by reallocations and collaboration; abolish Police and Crime Commissioners; Local Policing Commitment; new Police Standards Authority and Chartered Officers; stronger diversity recruitment. Replace low‑level cautions with payback orders; expand restorative and youth justice collaboration; integrate drug treatment; ban psychoactive “legal highs”; tougher child‑protection powers and a cross‑government unit; prisons focused on rehabilitation with professional standards; Victims’ Law. Restore stronger terror controls; mandatory de‑radicalisation for returnees; update investigatory powers with enhanced oversight; overhaul Prevent; stronger hate‑crime laws.

- Culture, sport, environment, rural: Creative education entitlement; free national museum entry; more creative apprenticeships; fans’ voice and board seats at football clubs; 5% of league TV income to grassroots. Climate adaptation plan and flood prevention; local air‑quality powers; keep forests public; enhance habitats; end the badger cull; strengthen animal‑welfare laws; long‑term food, farm and fisheries strategy and a stronger supermarket watchdog.

- Governance and devolution: People‑led Constitutional Convention; replace the House of Lords with an elected Senate; consider English‑only committee stages; English Devolution Act with £30bn and wider local powers; retain growth business rates locally; fair funding and multi‑year budgets; local Public Accounts Committees; expand open data and digital government; votes at 16–17; improve voter registration; tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies; require large firms to publish gender pay gaps; implement press‑reform recommendations; local powers over payday lenders and betting terminals. Deliver further devolution to Scotland and Wales; support Northern Ireland institutions and shared prosperity.

- Europe, foreign, defence, development, climate: Remain engaged in a reformed EU; no transfer of powers without a referendum lock; multilateral approach to security (criteria‑based use of force), two‑state solution in the Middle East, continued support for Afghanistan; Asia strategy; envoys for religious freedom and LGBT rights. Strategic Defence and Security Review in year one; strengthen the Armed Forces Covenant, veterans’ register and protections; support defence industry and cyber resilience; maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. Lead on an ambitious Paris agreement (net‑zero global emissions in the second half of the century, five‑year reviews); keep 0.7% GNI for development focused on the poorest, women and children; establish a Centre for Universal Health Coverage; expand tax transparency, anti‑corruption and ethical supply chains.
